text:
devon: Heads-up — after the long-context perf run last night I see steady KV cache memory growth and a growing free-list of tiny holes. Not a huge leak, more like fragmentation + lots of small free chunks not being reused.

maya: Ugh. Is this the 4k->16k context test or the prod-like mixed length?

devon: Mixed lengths. Repro locally with bench_kv --ctx-mix=varied --dur=4h shows mem up ~18% over baseline and tail latency creeping up.

perf-bot: snapshot: {alloc_total: 24.1GB, kv_live: 18.3GB, free_slabs: 3.6GB, small_fragments(<512): 1.8GB, fragmentation_ratio: 0.24} — profile_id=run-2026-05-02-03

sam: fragmentation_ratio 0.24 is high but not catastrophic. Where are the free blocks located? Many tiny ones?

devon: Yeah most free fragments are <1KB, but there are also gaps of ~8KB sprinkled. allocator uses power-of-two size classes starting at 64B. Suspect internal rounding + egregious reuse pattern for short-lived prompts.

ryan: Could be allocation churn from system prompts and tool-calling kernels that create/destroy many KV slices per token. We saw similar with the old slab when blocksize was 16KB vs 4KB.

maya: Idea: try a two-pronged experiment — 1) reduce micro-allocation overhead by increasing smallest size class to 128B and coalescing adjacent free microblocks, 2) add opportunistic compaction pass during idle windows (merge contiguous free blocks into larger free slabs).

devon: Agree. I sketched a small compactor prototype. Pseudo:```
// on idle, iterate free list by address
for (run over free_blocks) {
  if (adjacent(prev, cur)) merge(prev, cur);
} // also update sizeclass lists
```
This is cheap if we only scan headers and skip busy ranges.

sam: Nice. We should also test switching allocator strategy: slab-only vs slab+buddy coexists. Buddy helps with variable-size coalescing but may fragment differently. Can we A/B them on a dedicated Dedicated pool?

devon: I can spin up a small dedicated node and run both. Plan: baseline, proto-compactor, and buddy-hybrid. Measure: peak RSS, fragmentation_ratio, tail latency (p99.95 generation).

perf-bot: queued job: bench_kv_abtest(run=1815056900) — will run 30m per variant and upload perf traces to /perf/kv/1815056900

maya: Also add an experiment toggling block_size tuning: 4KB base vs 16KB base for slab allocation. In earlier benchmarks 16KB reduced meta overhead but increased internal waste for many tiny allocations. Need data for our mixed workload.

ryan: One more thought — consider prefix-aware reuse: when a KV chunk is freed, tag it with promt_id and token_range. If a new allocation requests same size and prior prefix present, prefer reuse to keep cache locality and reduce copying. Might reduce fragmentation by improving reuse hit-rate.

devon: Worth trying but higher complexity. I'll run the baseline + compactor + buddy + blocksize experiments today, gather profiles. Assigning myself to run, @maya will review compaction safety checks, @sam will validate correctness for buddy integration.

maya: sg. I'll add invariants: compaction must preserve KV offsets for active sessions and must not move live pages. We'll implement a strict check mode first.

sam: I'll review test harness and add regression tests that hammer small allocations and long contexts concurrently.

devon: OK good plan. Will post run summary and perf-bot traces in this thread when done. Thanks. :thumbsup:
